discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 061609
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
1209 PM EDT Tue Oct 6 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry conditions are expected through this work week.

- After starting out with slightly below normal high temps,
  highs slightly above normal take over for the end of the work
  week.

- Cold this morning with lows dipping down to the upper 30s for
  some areas north of US-6.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 233 AM EDT Tue Oct 6 2026

Forecast on track. This morning lows shaping up as advertised. A
few locations north of US-6 is trending to reach down into the
upper 30s. Dew points have stayed elevated (mainly in the lower
40s) which will keep temperatures from dropping much further.
Current temps here at the forecast office is 45 degrees as of
2:30 AM EDT. 

Temperatures will rebound nicely later today with western
portions of the CWA getting into the lower 70s with slight upper
level ridging pushing across the Great Lakes region. Breezy
southerly winds with a few gusts to around 20 mph later today 
into Wednesday. Wednesday looks to be warmer yet with most 
locations reaching into the 70s and even a few locations mainly 
south and west parts of the area getting near the 80 degree 
mark. Another weak upper level trough will then push into the 
region by Thursday and this will bring a an increase in clouds 
and a shot of cooler temperatures for Thursday and Friday with 
highs in the upper 60s to low 70s each day. Temperatures warm 
once again this weekend into the beginning of next week with 
highs back into the 70s across the area with a few locations 
again getting close to 80. Precipitation chances remain nil 
through the forecast until late into this weekend for Sunday and
at this time looks to be only for the far southeastern portions
of the CWA with that tropical disturbance pushing northeastward
from TX and into the Ohio Valley.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 1208 PM EDT Tue Oct 6 2026

High pressure overhead continues to provide tranquil and dry 
conditions. Expect VFR ceilings through the TAF period (with 
very few clouds at all) with southwest winds between 5-10 knots.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Andersen
AVIATION...Johnson

spc.text:
SPC AC 061602

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1102 AM CDT Tue Oct 06 2026

   Valid 061630Z - 071200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR THE
   WEST-CENTRAL PART OF THE FLORIDA PENINSULA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   A Marginal Risk for a brief waterspout/tornado is forecast near the
   coast of the west-central part of the Florida Peninsula through
   tonight.

   ...Central Florida Peninsula...
   Radar mosaic shows a discontinuous cluster of showers/thunderstorms
   over the northeast Gulf associated with a weak surface low/frontal
   wave along a frontal zone draped across the central part of the FL
   Peninsula.  Model guidance continues to show a modest enlargement of
   the hodograph through the late afternoon and continuing into
   tonight.  Although tropospheric lapse rates will remain poor,
   sufficient heating in areas void of thicker clouds/rain will lead to
   weak destabilization across the central part of the Peninsula, as
   well as over the warm shelf waters west of Tampa Bay (200-500 J/kg
   MLCAPE).  Radar observations earlier this morning showed a few
   brief/transient supercell structures.  Expecting an episodic
   continuation of these convective characteristics to eventually
   migrate closer to the immediate coast this afternoon and perhaps
   linger into late tonight.  As a result, a brief waterspout/tornado
   will be possible near the coast of the west-central portion of the
   Peninsula.  

   Elsewhere, severe weather is not forecast.

   ..Smith/Karstens.. 10/06/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 060405

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1105 PM CDT Mon Oct 05 2026

   Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are not expected on Wednesday.

   ...Northern Great Lakes...
   An upper low will move slowly toward James Bay, with a broad area of
   cyclonic flow aloft extending from the Upper MS Valley across the
   Great Lakes and into the Northeast. A backside speed max aloft will
   nose into MI late in the day, and toward the Lower Great Lakes into
   Thursday morning. Cool temperatures aloft north of the midlevel
   speed max and minimal moisture may yield a few weak thunderstorms
   late in the day over parts of the Upper Great Lakes.

   ...Four Corners States...
   Cool midlevel temperatures will exist across the Four Corners
   states, east of the upper ridge axis over CA. Isolated general
   thunderstorms will be possible with day time heating in the weak
   flow regime. Locally strong gusts may occur during the peak heating
   hours.

   ...NE...
   During the evening, a slight increase in low-level warm advection
   will occur over the Central Plains, and a few thunderstorms will be
   possible over NE overnight. Although cool aloft, available moisture
   will limit instability overall.

   ...FL...
   High pressure will maintain stable surface conditions over the
   southern Plains and Southeast, the exception being the FL Peninsula
   where scattered showers and thunderstorms will be possible.
   Instability and shear will not favor severe storms.

   ..Jewell.. 10/06/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 060509

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1209 AM CDT Tue Oct 06 2026

   Valid 081200Z - 091200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are not expected on Thursday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper low will move slowly into western Quebec on Thursday, with
   a broad area of cyclonic flow aloft from the northern Plains across
   the Great Lakes and into the Northeast. Low-topped convective
   showers may occur over parts of the upper Great Lakes by virtue of
   cold temperatures aloft.

   To the south, high pressure will maintain dry conditions over much
   of the Southeast, the exception being FL where a moist air mass and
   daytime heating will support scattered afternoon thunderstorms. 

   To the west, isolated weak thunderstorms may occur during the
   afternoon over parts of the Four Corners states, and overnight from
   eastern NE into northwest MO. Here, moisture will be the limiting
   factor to any elevated hail chances.

   ..Jewell.. 10/06/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
